proofs.proof_tex:
Let \((G,s,c)\) be any finite simple bow-free singleton-target instance in the stated class.  Thus \(c(v)\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) for every \(v\in V^{-}\), \(r(G,s)\leq 3\), and \(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\).  Choose \(R_0\in\mathcal C(G,s)\).  By Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\), there is a hedge \(F\) such that \(\{s\}\subsetneq F\) and \(R_0=F\setminus\{s\}\), so \(R_0\neq\varnothing\).  Finiteness and positivity give
\[
 m_0:=\min_{v\in R_0}c(v)>0.
\]
For every vector \(y\) feasible for the relaxation in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}covering\mbox{-}lp}\), nonnegativity of \(y\), the constraint indexed by \(R_0\), and the definition of \(m_0\) imply
\[
 \sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v
 \geq \sum_{v\in R_0}c(v)y_v
 \geq m_0\sum_{v\in R_0}y_v
 \geq m_0>0.
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)>0\), so the displayed ratio is well defined.  By Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}rounding}\), there is a feasible intervention \(A_t\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq 2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\) minimizes over all feasible interventions, whence
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)
 \leq \sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)
 \leq 2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
\]
Division by the strictly positive LP value proves
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)}{\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)}\leq 2
\]
for every instance in the full weighted class.

For the matching lower bound, fix \(n\geq2\), equip \(K_n\) with any total order, form its private-guard expansion \(G_{K_n}\), and assign unit cost to every vertex in \(V^{-}\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) shows that this is a finite simple bow-free singleton-target instance, that its bidirected subgraph is a tree of radius at most two, and that
\[
 \mathcal C(G_{K_n},s)
 =\bigl\{\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}:e=\{u,v\}\in E(K_n)\bigr\}.
\]
Because \(E(K_n)\neq\varnothing\), the same theorem gives \(r(G_{K_n},s)=3\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)=\tau(K_n).
\]
Any set of at most \(n-2\) vertices omits two vertices and therefore fails to cover their edge, whereas deleting any one vertex leaves a cover of all edges.  Consequently \(\tau(K_n)=n-1\).

Set \(y_{x_u}=1/2\) for every \(u\in U\) and \(y_{z_e}=0\) for every \(e\in E(K_n)\).  The displayed description of the clutter makes every covering constraint equal to \(1/2+1/2+0=1\), so this vector is feasible and has unit-cost objective \(n/2\).  Conversely, for any feasible \(y\), summing the constraint
\[
 y_{x_u}+y_{x_v}+y_{z_e}\geq1
\]
over all \(e=\{u,v\}\in E(K_n)\) counts each \(x_u\) exactly \(n-1\) times and yields
\[
 (n-1)\sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}+\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq \binom n2.
\]
After division by \(n-1>0\),
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}
 +\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq \frac n2.
\]
Since \(n\geq2\) and every \(y_{z_e}\geq0\), the unit-cost objective obeys
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}+\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq \frac n2.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)=n/2\), and therefore
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
 {\operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
 =\frac{n-1}{n/2}=2-\frac2n.
\]
These unit-cost radius-two-tree instances belong to the full weighted class.  Their ratios converge to two, so the supremum is at least two; the preceding universal upper bound shows that it is exactly two.

Finally assume \(\mathsf{UGC}\), fix \(\epsilon>0\), and suppose for contradiction that a polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation exists on the narrower subclass of unit-cost instances with nonempty clutter, rank at most three, and a radius-two bidirected tree.  Given any finite simple source graph \(H\) with at least one edge, construct \(G_H\) and assign unit costs.  By Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\), the resulting instance lies in that subclass.  If the assumed algorithm returns a feasible intervention \(A\), the polynomial-time guard-replacement map in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\) returns a vertex cover \(C_A\) with \(|C_A|\leq |A|\); the same theorem gives \(\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)=\tau(H)\).  Therefore
\[
 |C_A|
 \leq |A|
 \leq (2-\epsilon)\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)
 =(2-\epsilon)\tau(H).
\]
For an edgeless \(H\), the empty set is an optimal vertex cover, so this construction together with that trivial case would be a polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation for Minimum Vertex Cover on all finite simple graphs.  This contradicts Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ugc\mbox{-}vertex\mbox{-}cover\mbox{-}hardness}\).  Hence, under \(\mathsf{UGC}\), no such approximation algorithm exists on the stated narrower subclass.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The supremum of \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)/\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\) over all positive-rational-cost finite simple bow-free singleton-target instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and \(\mathcal C(G,s)\neq\varnothing\) equals two. For every \(n\geq2\), the unit-cost private-guard expansion \(G_{K_n}\), formed using any total order, has a radius-two bidirected tree and ratio \(2-2/n\). Under \(\mathsf{UGC}\), for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\), no polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation exists even on the narrower subclass of unit-cost instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\), nonempty residual clutter, and a radius-two bidirected tree.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing weighted rank-three rounding theorem proves the upper bound for every positive-rational-cost instance in the full promised class; unit-cost private-guard expansions of complete graphs lie inside that class and converge to the same bound. The unit-cost and radius-two-tree restrictions therefore belong only to the matching lower-bound family and the transferred \(\mathsf{UGC}\) hardness subclass, not to the integrality-gap supremum's ambient class.

prose_updates.tldr: Rank three is the first nonzero minimal residual-hedge rank for finite simple bow-free singleton-target ADMGs, and four-vertex hedges are exactly complementary directed and bidirected spanning paths. A one-private-guard expansion realizes the edge clutter of every ordered simple graph, yielding unit-cost \(\mathsf{NP}\)- and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness on radius-two bidirected trees. Under the promise \(r(G,s)\leq3\), the path classification partitions every minimal residual across target parents and spouses; after polynomial enumeration under that promise, this yields a deterministic weighted factor-two LP rounding algorithm. Consequently, the weighted natural-covering-LP integrality-gap supremum over all positive-rational-cost instances in the promised class with nonempty residual clutter is exactly two; unit-cost complete-graph expansions witness the lower bound, and the Khot--Regev threshold transfers under \(\mathsf{UGC}\) on the narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. The promised enumerator and optimizer-or-rank-violation interface support existing exact solvers without claiming an unrestricted rank-three recognition algorithm.

project_justification.gap: The published minimum-cost intervention-design frontier jumps from polynomial solvability at residual size two to unrestricted logarithmic hardness, but it does not identify the first nonempty finite simple bow-free singleton-target rank, the exact weighted natural-LP gap at that boundary, or the approximation threshold on a graphically sparse hard subclass.
project_justification.niche: Rank-three hedge clutters are not arbitrary three-uniform clutters: every minimal residual crosses the target-parent and target-spouse partition. This structure controls every positive-rational-cost instance under the rank promise, while private guards still realize every graph edge clutter inside the narrower unit-cost class whose bidirected graph is a radius-two tree.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the four-vertex obstruction classification and exact private-guard representation, transfers objective-preserving hardness, and establishes that the weighted natural-covering-LP integrality-gap supremum is exactly two over all positive-rational-cost rank-three-promise instances with nonempty residual clutter. Complete-graph gadgets supply the matching sequence, and \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional \(2-\epsilon\) hardness holds on the narrower unit-cost radius-two-tree subclass. Promised enumeration and a certifying optimizer-or-rank-violation interface are provided without asserting unrestricted recognition of the rank promise.

prose_updates.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl supply the complete hedge obstruction used to interpret residual hitting as causal identification. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash formulate minimum-cost intervention design as minimum-weight hedge hitting, prove unrestricted hardness, and settle bounded residual size through two; their boundary is continued here at the first nonzero finite simple bow-free singleton-target rank. Elahi and coauthors replace explicit hedge enumeration by WPMAX-SAT and ILP and leave approximation algorithms open, making their RC2 and Gurobi workflow an immediate computational consumer. Nemhauser and Trotter provide the classical half-integral vertex-cover geometry that informs the argument, while the parent-spouse threshold proof here acts directly on weighted causal residuals and yields the factor-two upper bound over the full positive-rational-cost rank-three-promise class. Alimonti and Kann provide cubic vertex-cover \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hardness, and Khot and Regev provide the conditional factor-two lower bound transferred to the narrower unit-cost radius-two-bidirected-tree subclass by the exact private-guard realization. Singh's LP-gap formula motivates the complete-graph sequence witnessing the matching supremum, but no sharpening of that source result is claimed. Fernau's explicit-hypergraph branching informs only the scoped bounded-cardinality routine; neither that routine nor the promised enumerator is presented as unrestricted rank-three recognition.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The factor-two algorithm is promise-based: polynomial enumeration is guaranteed after \(r(G,s)\leq3\) is supplied, but it does not recognize that promise, and a successful optimizer run is not a certificate that the rank bound holds. The \(O(3^k)\) exact-search guarantee also requires a supplied cardinality bound \(k\); it is not an unconstrained weighted parameterization by an unknown optimum cardinality. Finite-sample allocation and statistical estimation from acquired experiments remain outside this combinatorial identification-design result.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact weighted integrality-gap supremum ranges over all positive-rational-cost finite simple bow-free singleton-target instances with \(r(G,s)\leq3\) and nonempty residual clutter. Its matching sequence and the \(\mathsf{UGC}\)-conditional approximation lower bound use the narrower unit-cost private-guard subclass whose bidirected graph is a radius-two tree. General positivity-based equivalence between hedge hitting and interventional identification, source complexity theorems, and rational LP solution are imported. The complexity of recognizing rank at most three, planar bounded-degree causal realizability, rank-four realizability, finite-sample allocation, and solver speedups remain open. Weighted \(O(3^k)\) exact search is asserted only for a supplied cardinality bound.
